    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"C{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):

    for i, well_name in enumerate(well_names):
        well = plate[well_name]
        lib = libraries[i]
        well.load_liquid(liquid=lib, volume=50)
    
    # Select destination tube
    destination_tube = tubes["A1"]
    
    # Group wells into chunks of 8
    chunk_size = 8
    num_chunks = len(well_names) // chunk_size

    p20_multi.drop_tip()

tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {
    "protocolName": "Pool 5 ul from each of 48 indexed sequencing libraries into a single 1.5 ml tube",
    "apiLevel": "2.19"
}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tip_rack = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 1)
    tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 2)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 3)
    
    # Load pipette
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tip_rack])
    
    # Define liquids
    libraries = []
    for i in range(1, 49):
        lib = protocol.define_liquid(name=f"library {i}", description=None)
        libraries.append(lib)
    
    # Generate well names A1..D12 (48 wells)
    well_names = []
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"A{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"B{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"C{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"D{col}")
    
    # Load each library into its well with 50 ul starting volume
    for i, well_name in enumerate(well_names):
        well = plate[well_name]
        lib = libraries[i]
        well.load_liquid(liquid=lib, volume=50)
    
    # Select destination tube
    destination_tube = tubes["A1"]
    
    # Pick up tip once
    p20.pick_up_tip()
    
    # Process each well individually
    for well_name in well_names:
        well = plate[well_name]
        # Aspirate 5 ul from the well
        p20.aspirate(5, well)
        # Dispense 5 ul into the destination tube
        p20.dispense(5, destination_tube)
    
    # Drop tip
    p20.drop_tip()"}

protocol.py: 2 biology problems (2 warnings).

1. WARNING CONTAM-STOCK: A used tip went into a stock: 47 stocks
   line 50:  p20.aspirate(5, well)
   At line 50 the tip went into library 2 (well A2 in slot 3), library 3 (well A3 in slot
   3), library 4 (well A4 in slot 3), library 5 (well A5 in slot 3) and 43 more while it
   still carried library 1 (well A1 in slot 3), library 2 (well A2 in slot 3), library 3
   (well A3 in slot 3), library 4 (well A4 in slot 3) and 43 more from an earlier step (this
   line did it 47 times). A tip that has touched one liquid leaves a little of it in the
   next liquid it touches, so these stocks now hold material that does not belong there. The
   protocol does not draw from them again, so this run is not harmed, but what is left in
   the stock is no longer clean for the next run.
   Affected: wells A2, A3, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, A9 and 39 more in slot 3.
   Fix: Pick up a fresh tip before line 50 goes into the stock. Or change the order: hand
   out the shared liquid first, while the tip is still clean, and add the other liquids
   afterwards with a fresh tip each.
   Source: Lab Manager: minimizing cross-contamination in automated liquid handling
           https://www.labmanager.com/minimizing-cross-contamination-in-automated-liquid-handling-workflows-35194
   Source: WHO: dos and don'ts for molecular testing
           https://www.who.int/teams/global-malaria-programme/case-management/diagnosis/nucleic-acid-amplification-based-diagnostics/dos-and-don-ts-for-molecular-testing
   [28e72ff8b3d9]

well)
   line 52:  p20.dispense(5, destination_tube)
   At line 52 the robot added library 48 to tube A1 in slot 2, which already held library 1,
   library 2, library 3, library 4 and 43 more. The addition was 2% of the well, nothing
   mixed the well afterwards, and the run ended with it that way. Two liquids layered in a
   small well do not mix on their own, so what the well holds is not at the concentration
   you calculated. The liquid added last is a sample, so nothing else in the workflow will
   mix it: a normalisation or a pool left like this is not what it says it is.

tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {
    "protocolName": "Pool 5 ul from each of 48 indexed sequencing libraries into a single 1.5 ml tube",
    "apiLevel": "2.19"
}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tip_rack = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 1)
    tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 2)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 3)
    
    # Load pipette
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tip_rack])
    
    # Define liquids
    libraries = []
    for i in range(1, 49):
        lib = protocol.define_liquid(name=f"library {i}", description=None)
        libraries.append(lib)
    
    # Generate well names A1..D12 (48 wells)
    well_names = []
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"A{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"B{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"C{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"D{col}")
    
    # Load each library into its well with 50 ul starting volume
    for i, well_name in enumerate(well_names):
        well = plate[well_name]
        lib = libraries[i]
        well.load_liquid(liquid=lib, volume=50)
    
    # Select destination tube
    destination_tube = tubes["A1"]
    
    # Process each well individually
    for well_name in well_names:
        well = plate[well_name]
        # Pick up a fresh tip for each well to avoid cross‑contamination
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        # Aspirate 5 ul from the well
        p20.aspirate(5, well)
        # Dispense 5 ul into the destination tube
        p20.dispense(5, destination_tube)
        # Drop the tip
        p20.drop_tip()
    
    # Mix the pooled tube to ensure homogeneity
    p20.mix(5, 10, destination_tube)"}

tool_calls.name: write_protocol
tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {
    "protocolName": "Pool 5 ul from each of 48 indexed sequencing libraries into a single 1.5 ml tube",
    "apiLevel": "2.19"
}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tip_rack = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 1)
    tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 2)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 3)
    
    # Load pipettes
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tip_rack])
    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "left", tip_racks=[tip_rack])
    
    # Define liquids
    libraries = []
    for i in range(1, 49):
        lib = protocol.define_liquid(name=f"library {i}", description=None)
        libraries.append(lib)
    
    # Generate well names A1..D12 (48 wells)
    well_names = []
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"A{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"B{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"C{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"D{col}")
    
    # Load each library into its well with 50 ul starting volume
    for i, well_name in enumerate(well_names):
        well = plate[well_name]
        lib = libraries[i]
        well.load_liquid(liquid=lib, volume=50)
    
    # Select destination tube
    destination_tube = tubes["A1"]
    
    # Process each well individually with p20
    for i, well_name in enumerate(well_names):
        well = plate[well_name]
        # Pick up a fresh tip for each well
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        # Aspirate 5 ul from the well
        p20.aspirate(5, well)
        # Dispense 5 ul into the destination tube
        p20.dispense(5, destination_tube)
        # Drop tip
        p20.drop_tip()
    
    # Mix the pooled tube with p300
    p300.pick_up_tip()
    p300.mix(192, 5, destination_tube)
    p300.drop_tip()"}

tool_calls.arguments:
{"text": "from opentrons import protocol_api

metadata = {
    "protocolName": "Pool 5 ul from each of 48 indexed sequencing libraries into a single 1.5 ml tube",
    "apiLevel": "2.19"
}

def run(protocol: protocol_api.ProtocolContext):
    # Load labware
    tip_rack = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_96_tiprack_20ul", 1)
    tubes = protocol.load_labware("opentrons_24_tuberack_nest_1.5ml_snapcap", 2)
    plate = protocol.load_labware("nest_96_wellplate_200ul_flat", 3)
    
    # Load pipettes
    p20 = protocol.load_instrument("p20_single_gen2", "right", tip_racks=[tip_rack])
    p300 = protocol.load_instrument("p300_single_gen2", "left", tip_racks=[tip_rack])
    
    # Define liquids
    libraries = []
    for i in range(1, 49):
        lib = protocol.define_liquid(name=f"library {i}", description=None)
        libraries.append(lib)
    
    # Generate well names A1..D12 (48 wells)
    well_names = []
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"A{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"B{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"C{col}")
    for col in range(1, 13):
        well_names.append(f"D{col}")
    
    # Load each library into its well with 50 ul starting volume
    for i, well_name in enumerate(well_names):
        well = plate[well_name]
        lib = libraries[i]
        well.load_liquid(liquid=lib, volume=50)
    
    # Select destination tube
    destination_tube = tubes["A1"]
    
    # Process each well individually with p20
    for i, well_name in enumerate(well_names):
        well = plate[well_name]
        # Pick up a fresh tip for each well
        p20.pick_up_tip()
        # Aspirate 5 ul from the well
        p20.aspirate(5, well)
        # Dispense 5 ul into the destination tube
        p20.dispense(5, destination_tube)
        # Drop tip
        p20.drop_tip()
    
    # Mix the pooled tube with p300
    p300.pick_up_tip()
    p300.mix(192, 5, destination_tube)
    p300.drop_tip()"}

protocol.py: 1 biology problem (1 error).

1. ERROR PIPETTE-RANGE: 5 ul is below what the p300_single_gen2 can measure (20 ul at least)
   line 58:  p300.mix(192, 5, destination_tube)
   At line 58 the p300_single_gen2 is asked to draw 5 ul, below its minimum of 20 ul (this
   line did it 192 times). A pipette cannot measure less than its minimum: it draws the
   wrong amount, or nothing, and the volumes in this protocol only add up on paper. The
   simulator passes the move. Wells: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Affected: tube A1 in slot 2.
   Fix: Use a pipette whose range covers the volume (a p20 for 1 to 20 ul), or scale the
   reaction so every volume is at least the pipette's minimum.
   Source: Opentrons: pipette characteristics (volume ranges)
           https://docs.opentrons.com/v2/pipettes/characteristics.html
   Source: Integra: pipetting tips (work at 35 to 100% of nominal volume)
           https://www.integra-biosciences.com/united-states/en/pipetting-tips
   [c0cd375bc708]

can make the moves, not what they do to the liquids.
